finding: Experts rated LLM ideas as more novel than human ideas and not more feasible; LLM outputs showed less diversity.

title: On or Off Track: How (Broken) Streaks Affect Consumer Decisions
finding: An intact logged streak raises later engagement and a broken one lowers it, independent of actual behaviour; the drop eases when the streak can be repaired.
contested: Engagement outcome only; no learning measure.

title: Do “Brain-Training” Programs Work?
venue: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
population: Intervention studies cited by brain-training companies
finding: Extensive evidence of gains on trained tasks, less on closely related tasks, and little on distant tasks or everyday performance.

title: The misdirection of public policy: comparing and combining standardised effect sizes
finding: Standardized effect size depends on comparison group, sample range and measure, so league tables rank research designs more than interventions.

title: When Problem Solving Followed by Instruction Works: Evidence for Productive Failure
finding: Problem solving first gives a moderate advantage, larger with high fidelity to productive-failure design; the trend reverses for second to fifth graders.

effect.value: g = 0.36, 95% CI [0.20, 0.51]; 0.37 to 0.58 with high fidelity

contested: Contrasting trends for second to fifth graders, per the abstract.

title: To What Extent and Under Which Circumstances Are Growth Mind-Sets Important to Academic Achievement? Two Meta-Analyses
population: k = 273, N = 365,915 for the association; k = 43, N = 57,155 for interventions
finding: Both the mindset to achievement link and the intervention effect are weak; low-SES and at-risk students may benefit.

effect.value: Overall effects 'weak' in both meta-analyses

title: How Math Academy Creates its Knowledge Graph
Optimized, Individualized Spaced Repetition in Hierarchical Knowledge Structures
Mastery Learning Reconsidered
population: Group-based mastery learning in elementary and secondary schools, at least 4 weeks
finding: Best-evidence synthesis found no support on standardized measures and moderate effects on experimenter-made measures that did not persist.

effect.value: Essentially no effect on standardized achievement measures

contested: Contradicts Kulik, Kulik and Bangert-Drowns 1990 (ES 0.52, literature:kulik-kulik-bangert-drowns-1990-mastery-learning-meta-analysis).

title: A Quantitative Review of Performance Feedback in Organizational Settings (1998-2018)
finding: Feedback produced large effects across applications, including those meeting What Works Clearinghouse standards.
contested: Drawn from four journals; Kluger and DeNisi 1996 (10.1037/0033-2909.119.2.254) report a smaller average, with over one third of interventions lowering performance.

title: Leveraging "Khanmigo" Generative AI-Powered Tool for Personalized Tutoring to Learn Scientific Concepts
population: Students learning physics concepts in three conditions; n not given
finding: Khanmigo users scored higher than web-search users and comparable to paper-based instruction, with higher reported engagement.

title: Does performance improve following multisource feedback? a theoretical model, meta‐analysis, and review of empirical findings
finding: Improvement in direct report, peer and supervisor ratings after multisource feedback was small.

title: Learning Versus Performance: An Integrative Review
population: Review of motor and verbal learning research
finding: Performance during acquisition is an unreliable index of learning; some manipulations raise one and lower the other, and learners misread fluent performance as learning.

title: Google Effects on Memory: Cognitive Consequences of Having Information at Our Fingertips
finding: People remembered facts worse when they expected the file to be saved and remembered where to find them better.

title: Job Market Signaling
finding: Education can raise wages by signalling pre-existing ability to employers even if it adds no productivity.
contested: Clark and Martorell 2014 find little diploma signalling; Aryal et al. 2022 estimate 30%.

title: Cognitive Ease at a Cost: LLMs Reduce Mental Effort but Compromise Depth in Student Scientific Inquiry
population: Students on a scientific inquiry task; n not given
finding: LLM-assisted students reported lower mental effort and produced shallower inquiry outputs.

title: Gender differences in mathematics and science competitions: A systematic review
venue: Journal of Research in Science Teaching
population: Studies of math and science competitions; count not given
finding: Olympiads showed large gender gaps in participation in every subject except biology.

title: ITS on K-12 mathematical learning
population: K-12 math studies of intelligent tutoring; count not given
finding: ITS outperformed traditional classroom instruction by a small margin in K-12 math and underperformed human tutoring.

effect.value: g≈0.09 (ns); K-12 mathematics

title: ITS on college students' academic learning
population: College studies of intelligent tutoring; count not given
finding: ITS produced a small positive effect versus conventional classroom instruction and was statistically indistinguishable from human tutoring or small group instruction.

effect.value: g in the 0.3 range versus classroom instruction

title: On the Theory of Scales of Measurement
ChatGPT listed as author on research papers: many scientists disapprove
finding: Papers listing a generative AI tool as co-author drew objections, and publishers barred AI author credit while allowing disclosed assistive use.

title: Saving-Enhanced Memory: The Benefits of Saving on the Learning and Remembering of New Information
finding: Saving a first list improved recall of a second list, and the saved list was recalled worse.

title: The Effects of "Mandatory Volunteerism" on Intentions to Volunteer
population: College students in a field study and an experiment; n not given
finding: Students who felt unlikely to volunteer freely reported lower future intentions after a mandate than after a choice.

title: Sensecape: Enabling Multilevel Exploration and Sensemaking with Large Language Models
finding: An LLM-assisted canvas that lets users move between low-level notes and high-level summaries improves sensemaking over a flat chat interface.

title: Keep it coherent: A meta-analysis of the seductive details effect
Algorithm SM-18
Fish Oil, Raynaud's Syndrome, and Undiscovered Public Knowledge
finding: Two literatures that never cited each other jointly implied a hypothesis that a later trial supported.

title: An interactive system for finding complementary literatures: a stimulus to scientific discovery
finding: Describes Arrowsmith, the working implementation of the ABC model as an interactive tool, and reports it surfacing further candidate connections beyond fish oil/Raynaud's.

title: The Virtual Lab of AI Agents Designs New SARS-CoV-2 Nanobodies
population: AI agent team with wet-lab validation
finding: A team of role-specialized AI agents, each with a defined expert persona, plus human checkpoints produced a result validated by wet-lab experiment.

title: Cognitive Load During Problem Solving: Effects on Learning
population: Students on algebra and geometry problems in two experiments; n not given
finding: Students who studied worked examples solved later transfer problems faster and more accurately than students who practiced conventional problem solving.

title: Cognitive architecture and instructional design
Why Minimally Guided Teaching Techniques Do Not Work: A Reply to Commentaries
finding: The authors hold that the commentaries describe guided methods and so concede the point; they ask for randomized, controlled comparisons.
contested: Closes the 2006 to 2007 Educational Psychologist exchange without agreement.

title: Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later
finding: Summarises twenty years of cognitive load effects and their boundary conditions.
contested: de Jong 2010 argues the load types are not separately measurable.

title: MOLIERE: Automatic Biomedical Hypothesis Generation System
finding: Combines a heterogeneous biomedical knowledge network with topic modeling to rank candidate A-B-C connections, evaluated by discovery-date holdout against later-published links.

title: Learning Trajectory Based Instruction
finding: A trajectory links a goal, a developmental path and matched tasks, is grounded in observed student reasoning, and needs ongoing formative assessment to place each student.

title: Exploring internal stickiness: Impediments to the transfer of best practice within the firm
population: 122 best-practice transfers in eight companies, 271 observations
finding: The main barriers were knowledge-related: low absorptive capacity of the recipient, causal ambiguity and an arduous relationship between source and recipient. Motivation mattered less.

title: Examining Summer Laboratory Research Apprenticeships for High School Students as a Factor in Entry to MD/PhD Programs at Matriculation
population: 236,432 individuals tracked to medical school matriculation
finding: Apprenticeships were associated with MD/PhD matriculation nearly a decade later.

effect.value: association, size not recorded internally; n = 236,432

title: Do Team and Individual Debriefs Enhance Performance? A Meta-Analysis
venue: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society
finding: Debriefs improved effectiveness by about 25%, with similar effects for teams and individuals and for simulated and real settings.

effect.value: d = .67; 46 samples; N = 2,136; about 25% improvement over control

title: A Meta-Analytic Review of Behavior Modeling Training.
finding: Effects were largest for learning, smaller for job behaviour and smaller again for results. Transfer was greatest with mixed models, trainee-generated scenarios, goal setting and trained supervisors.

title: The effects of interleaved practice
How is the Duolingo English Test scored
Artificial Intelligence, Scientific Discovery, and Product Innovation
population: Claimed: 1,018 scientists in a US firm R&D lab
finding: Withdrawn. The paper claimed 44% more materials discovered and 39% more patent filings.
contested: arXiv administrators withdrew the paper over concerns about the validity of the data and incomplete Institutional Review Board requirements (arXiv comment field for 2412.17866).

title: The Uses of Argument
finding: An argument has a claim, grounds, warrant, backing, qualifier and rebuttal, and its soundness depends on the field.

title: Seshat: The Global History Databank
venue: Cliodynamics: The Journal of Quantitative History and Cultural Evolution
finding: Describes a structured, expert-and-research-assistant-populated databank of historical and archaeological variables across societies, explicit about its double-coding and expert-review process for data quality.

title: Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases: Biases in judgments reveal some heuristics of thinking under uncertainty.
finding: Three heuristics are economical and lead to systematic, predictable errors in probability judgment.

title: The Effects of Repetition on Incidental Vocabulary Learning: A Meta‐Analysis of Correlational Studies
finding: Encounters relate to incidental learning at a medium size.

effect.value: r = .34 (45 effect sizes, N = 1,918)

title: International Standard Classification of Education: ISCED 2011
finding: Education is defined as the processes by which societies deliberately transmit their accumulated information, knowledge, understanding, attitudes, values, skills, competencies and behaviours across generations; it involves communication designed to bring about learning.

title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 26
finding: "Education shall be directed to the full development of the human personality and to the strengthening of respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms." (Article 26.2).

title: From promise to practice: harnessing generative AI to improve foundational learning in Sub-Saharan Africa
finding: Pilots show promise on narrow tasks; deployments with structured teacher support outperform chatbot-style ones, and infrastructure, language and cost limit scale.

title: When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
population: Studies of human-AI combinations; count not given in the record
finding: Human-AI combinations beat the better of either alone on decision tasks and fell short on content creation.

title: Applying Centrality Measures to the Course Prerequisite Network Analysis of the Undergraduate Civil Engineering Curriculum
finding: A small set of courses had centrality far above the median, concentrated in the early-to-middle sequence.

title: Effects of Feedback in a Computer-Based Learning Environment on Students’ Learning Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis
population: 40 studies, 70 effect sizes in computer-based environments
finding: Explanations beat showing the correct answer, which beats right or wrong marking.

effect.value: Elaborated 0.49; correct answer 0.32; right or wrong only 0.05; range -0.78 to 2.29

title: Are you interested? A meta-analysis of relations between vocational interests and employee performance and turnover.
finding: Single interest scales had small validities, larger when the scale matched the specific job.

effect.value: .14 job performance; .26 training performance; -.19 turnover intentions; -.15 actual turnover; job-specific scales .23 for job performance versus .10 for single RIASEC interests

title: Inter‐ and Intra‐Organizational Knowledge Transfer: A Meta‐Analytic Review and Assessment of its Antecedents and Consequences
finding: Knowledge, organization and network characteristics each relate to transfer, and context and direction moderate the relationships.

title: The Relative Effectiveness of Human Tutoring, Intelligent Tutoring Systems, and Other Tutoring Systems
population: Studies of human tutoring and tutoring systems; count not given
finding: Step-based tutoring systems were about as effective as human tutors; answer-based systems were weaker.

effect.value: d = 0.76 step-based ITS; d = 0.79 human tutors; d = 0.31 answer-based ITS
human tutoring d≈0.79; ITS d≈0.76; answer-based CAI d≈0.31
about 0.75 to 1 SD step-based, about 0.3 SD answer-based; tutoring-system studies

title: Learning Dashboards: An Overview and Future Research Opportunities
finding: Calls for dashboards that support reflection and action, not just awareness, as the design bar.

title: Learning Analytics Dashboard Applications
finding: Most dashboards had no published study of their effect on teaching decisions or outcomes.

title: Duolingo Effectiveness Study: Final Report
population: Adult Spanish learners using Duolingo for about eight weeks
finding: A commissioned pre-post study with no control group reported gains on a placement test per hour of study.
contested: Krashen's critique notes attrition (90 of 156 finished), an older and more educated sample, and Duolingo funding.

title: Two-Sigma Tutoring: Separating Science Fiction from Science Fact
population: Review of Bloom 1984 and later tutoring evidence
finding: Bloom's figure came from two dissertations using narrow tests, extra feedback and trained tutors; 'About one-third of a standard deviation seems to be the typical effect of an intense, well-designed program evaluated against broad tests.'

effect.value: About one third of an SD typical; Cohen, Kulik and Kulik 1982 about 0.33 SD; Nickow et al. 2020 0.37 SD, none of 96 studies reached two sigma

title: Mind in Society: The Development of Higher Psychological Processes
Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims
finding: Introduces SciFact, a claim-verification task pairing a claim with a support or refute label and a rationale sentence from the source.

title: MultiVerS: Improving scientific claim verification with weak supervision and full-document context
finding: Shows verification accuracy improves by reading the full source document instead of isolated sentences, and that weak supervision from related tasks helps more than more in-domain labels.

title: Quality Matters: The Expulsion of Professors and the Consequences for PhD Student Outcomes in Nazi Germany
population: Mathematics PhD students in Germany before and after the dismissals of 1933
finding: Faculty quality determined short-run and long-run PhD student outcomes.

effect.value: One SD rise in faculty quality: +13 percentage points probability of publishing the dissertation in a top journal; +10 points becoming full professor; +16 points positive lifetime citations; +6.3 lifetime citations

contested: One field and one historical setting.

title: Early-career setback and future career impact
population: Junior scientists near the NIH R01 funding threshold
finding: A near miss predicted more than a 10% chance of leaving the NIH system for good, and those who stayed outperformed narrow winners in the longer run.

effect.value: More than a 10% chance of disappearing permanently from the NIH system after a near miss

title: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
finding: An LLM pipeline that retrieves related papers, iteratively critiques its own generated idea against a novelty check, and shows measurable novelty gains over single-pass generation.

title: Scientific discovery in the age of artificial intelligence
population: Review of AI-for-science methods across fields
finding: The most mature results sit in representation learning and prediction; generation and closed-loop autonomy are early, and evaluation is a weak point across the field.

title: Tutor CoPilot: A Human-AI Approach for Scaling Real-Time Expertise
finding: Students of tutors with the copilot mastered more topics, with the largest gains for lower-rated tutors; tutors shifted toward guiding questions.

effect.value: +4 percentage points mastery overall, p < 0.01; +9 points for lower-rated tutors

title: People Mistake the Internet's Knowledge for Their Own
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Searching raised self-rated unaided knowledge and confidence for future questions; the effect was stronger for smooth search.

title: How Effective Are Intentional Vocabulary‐Learning Activities? A Meta‐Analysis
finding: Intentional study gives large immediate gains that fall by a third to a half at a delay.

effect.value: Immediate 60.1% meaning recall, 58.5% form recall; delayed 39.4% and 25.1%; activities range 18.4% to 77.0%

title: Effectiveness of career choice interventions: A meta-analytic replication and extension
finding: Meta-analytic replication and extension of earlier findings on career choice interventions.

title: The Aims of Education
Expectancy–Value Theory of Achievement Motivation
population: Review of child and adolescent studies
finding: Ability beliefs and task values change with age and predict performance and choice of activity.

title: How Can Educators Teach Critical Thinking?
Critical Thinking: Why Is It So Hard to Teach?
Historical problem solving
population: Expert historians and students; n not given
finding: Expert historians sourced and corroborated documents before evaluating their content; students read for content first and trusted the material's apparent authority.

title: Lateral Reading and the Nature of Expertise: Reading Less and Learning More When Evaluating Digital Information
population: Historians, undergraduates and professional fact checkers; n not given
finding: Fact checkers left the site to check other sources first and judged more accurately and faster than historians or students who stayed on the page.

title: Teaching for Understanding: Linking Research with Practice
population: Teachers across subjects and grades studied over multiple years; n not given
finding: A four-part framework of generative topics, understanding goals, understanding performances and ongoing assessment; implementation quality was the strongest predictor of improvement.

title: The Power of Feedback Revisited: A Meta-Analysis of Educational Feedback Research
finding: Feedback has a medium average effect with high heterogeneity; it cannot be treated as one treatment.
contested: Lowers the Hattie and Timperley figure near 0.79 held in the corpus.

title: The Role of Tutoring in Problem Solving
venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry 17(2), 89-100

title: SuperMemo 2: Algorithm (from Optimization of learning, Master's thesis, University of Technology in Poznan)
finding: Intervals are I(1) = 1 day, I(2) = 6 days, then I(n) = I(n-1) x EF, with the easiness factor starting at 2.5, adjusted by a 0 to 5 self-grade and floored at 1.3. The formula 'was constructed heuristically'.

title: Large teams develop and small teams disrupt science and technology
population: Tens of millions of papers and patents
finding: Small teams produce more disruptive work and large teams more developmental work, after controlling for members' citation histories.

title: Exploring Young Children's Engagement in Joint Reading With a Conversational Agent
finding: Young children treat a conversational reading agent as a social partner, addressing it and expecting reciprocal attention.

title: Same Benefits, Different Communication Patterns: Comparing Children's Reading With a Conversational Agent vs. a Human Partner
population: Children reading with an AI or human partner; n not given
finding: Children reading with an AI partner showed comparable learning gains to reading with a human partner but different turn-taking patterns.

title: On the Dempster-Shafer framework and new combination rules
finding: Shows Dempster's original combination rule produces counterintuitive results (near-certainty from weak, conflicting sources) and proposes alternative combination rules that handle conflicting evidence more sensibly.

title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
finding: One system-produced paper was accepted at a peer-reviewed workshop; topics and budgets were still set by humans.

title: Promises and challenges of generative artificial intelligence for human learning
finding: A review arguing generative AI's fluency can be mistaken for learning, and that unmonitored use risks substituting AI output for a learner's own cognitive work.

title: To What Extent Does the Involvement Load Hypothesis Predict Incidental L2 Vocabulary Learning? A Meta‐Analysis
finding: The hypothesis predicts learning but explains little variance.

effect.value: 15.0% of variance on immediate and 5.1% on delayed posttests

title: Testing (quizzing) boosts classroom learning: A systematic and meta-analytic review.
finding: Classroom testing raises achievement to a medium extent; exposure, transfer-appropriate processing and motivation each explain part of it.

title: Large Language Models for Automated Open-domain Scientific Hypotheses Discovery
finding: Frames hypothesis generation as inference from raw observations rather than from curated background literature, and reports LLMs can produce social-science hypotheses judged plausible by annotators.

title: A Stochastic Shortest Path Algorithm for Optimizing Spaced Repetition Scheduling
venue: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
population: 220 million memory logs from a language app
finding: The scheduler cut review cost against prior methods in simulation on the collected logs.

effect.value: 12.6% performance improvement over state-of-the-art methods
~20-30% fewer reviews for equal retention (Anki users); +12.6% over prior schedulers (220M MaiMemo review logs)

contested: Outcome is simulated cost on logs; no learner trial.

title: A national experiment reveals where a growth mindset improves achievement
population: Nationally representative sample of US ninth graders, preregistered
finding: Grades improved among lower-achieving students and advanced mathematics enrolment rose; effects held where peer norms supported the message.
contested: Macnamara and Burgoyne 2023 find d = 0.05 overall and near zero in the best studies.

title: Examining Adult-Child Interactions in Intergenerational Participatory Design
finding: Adults in co-design sessions with children default to leading unless the session is structured to hand children control.

title: Wordcraft: Story Writing With Large Language Models
finding: Writers using an LLM co-writer report the tool is most useful for unblocking, not for producing final prose they keep as-is.

title: Evaluating everyday explanations
population: Participants rating real explanations; n not given
finding: Ratings track coherence with prior belief and coverage of the fact; people recognize good explanations better than they generate them.

title: Exploring the impact of gamification on students’ academic performance: A comprehensive meta‐analysis of studies from the year 2008 to 2023
finding: Gamification showed a positive effect on academic performance.
contested: Larger than the g = 0.49 of Sailer and Homner 2020.

title: Hypothesis Generation with Large Language Models
venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on NLP for Science (NLP4Science)
finding: Refined hypotheses improved classifier accuracy over single-pass prompting and were rated more interpretable.

title: Extracting Prerequisite Relations Among Concepts in Wikipedia
venue: 2019 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
finding: A neural model on link, length and category features beat baselines; accuracy varied by domain.
